Decorative ironwork was already prominent in
the streets of Charleston, hundreds of gates, fences, and
railings featured curves, curlicues, and other flourishes.
Bending and beating iron into graceful shapes are never
easy to do, but Simmons mastered it. Soon his work
surpassed the quality of the city’s older pieces.
Moreover, Simmons broadened the cultural scope
of Charleston’s ironwork. The city’s iron pieces had
historically reflected European design, and Simmons
excelled in that style. But his mentor, whom, like
Simmons, was African American, also exposed him
to a centuries-old West African ironworking tradition.
